provenance.source: NECB 2025 Table 5.2.12.1 series, retrieved via the building-codes MCP (necb:2025). RE-VERIFIED against the post-hbix#88 MCP extraction 2026-08-02 (D-60): the letter map is -A unitary ACs & HPs, -G PTAC/PTHP, -K chillers, -N boilers, -O furnaces, -I VRF, -M plant heat pumps heating. The earlier map in this block ("-C PTAC/PTHP") came from a corrupted pre-fix extraction; -C is the water/evaporatively-cooled unitary table. Performance curves: vendored from openstudio-standards NECB2011/data/curves.json (origin; see curves[].notes).
provenance.note: Capacity match rule (ported from legacy model_find_object): row matches when minimum_capacity < capacity <= maximum_capacity, retried at 0.99x capacity on boundary misses; criteria keys absent from a row act as wildcards. Values re-verified against the post-hbix#88 MCP extraction 2026-08-02 (D-59/D-60): unitary_acs and heat_pumps = Table 5.2.12.1.-A, the small air-cooled bin reading "air conditioners AND heat pumps ... SEER 15" as an explicit class (D-59); PTAC/PTHP = Table -G (EER 11.9 / 14.1-1.0435xCap / 9.5; PTHP COPh 3.3/formula/2.9); heat_pumps_heating = Table -A (split-system small HSPF 7.8, single-package 7.4, COPh 3.3/3.2); chillers = Table -K Path B full-load COPc; boilers = Table -N; furnaces = Table -O (strict-side row choices documented). Vendored but INERT for the engine: the single-phase SEER2/EER2/HSPF2 rows (the subcategory never matches the Single Package lookup), the low-temperature COPh 2.25/2.05 rows (the -8.3 C behaviour comes from the reference part-load curves), and the Table 5.2.12.1.-M plant-heat-pump COPs. The 90.1-sourced heat_rejection family left this file under D-89: nothing read it, and the reference tower fan is set by apply_tower_rules from Table 5.2.12.2 plus the 8.4.5.11.(2)-(3) cell rules (D-26). IEER/IPLV/SCOP columns are not modeled: EnergyPlus carries full-load COP plus the reference part-load curves. Those part-load curves are this edition's own since D-89: part_load_fheatplc carries every FHeatPLC class Articles 8.4.6.2. and 8.4.6.3. publish (with a deferred_reason on each class no reference rule elects), part_load_curves maps an equipment class to the curve that represents it, and every boilers and furnaces row declares its part_load_curve_class instead of naming one curve for all of them.

part_load_fheatplc.formula: FHeatPLC = a + b(Qpartload/Qdesign) + c(Qpartload/Qdesign)^2 + d(Tw,return) + e(Tw,return)^2 + f(Qpartload/Qdesign)(Tw,return)
part_load_fheatplc.deferred_reason: not implemented: no reference rule elects condensing equipment, and this edition states the requirement over the part-load ratio AND the boiler return-hot-water temperature, for which the Code publishes no bounds. Retained here as the edition's published requirement (D-89).

curves.name: BOILER-PLF-MODULATING-necb2025

implements.error_grid: max relative error of the Linear interpolation against the exact rational PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR), sampled at PLR 0.0010 to 1.0000 step 0.0001: 0.7899 % at PLR 0.0014. The grid is finest where the rational is most convex (below PLR 0.05), and the boiler's engine minimum part-load ratio is raised to the first node (0.001) when lower, so every part-load ratio the engine can evaluate lies inside this domain.

curves.notes: Reference modulating boiler part-load factor for Article 8.4.6.2. This edition states the modulating requirement as a coefficient row of Table 8.4.6.2 (a 0.01798667, b 0.96742420, c 0.01545455), so the EnergyPlus normalized-boiler-efficiency multiplier is PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR) (the D-53 transform). The name is code-qualified because this edition's modulating content is its own (D-88).

curves.name: DXCOOL-REF-COOLEIRFT
curves.notes: Regenerated 2026-07-22 from 8.4.6.4.(7) via the exact degF->degC variable substitution; self-checks to ~1.0 at the 67F wb / 95F odb rating point. Replaces the legacy NECB 2011-derived surface whose twb terms deviated up to 1.95% off-rating (see scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.rb).  Governing requirement in this edition: Article 8.4.6.4.

curves.name: DXCOOL-REF-COOLPLFFPLR
curves.notes: Refit 2026-07-22: least-squares cubic of PLF(PLR) = PLR / EIR_FPLR(PLR) over PLR 0.25-1.0, from the 8.4.6.4.(5) EIR_FPLR cubic. Output clamped to [0.7, 1.0] (PLF > 1 is nonphysical; E+ guidance floor 0.7). A cubic cannot represent the rational target exactly: max implied-EIR deviation ~2.0% (the structural floor; was 3.70% with the legacy 0.7-floored refit). See scripts/necb_8_4_6_curve_probe.rb.  Governing requirement in this edition: Article 8.4.6.4.

curves.notes: Reference atmospheric furnace part-load factor for Article 8.4.6.3. The Code states FHeatPLC as a fuel-INPUT ratio (Fuel_partload = Fuel_rated x FHeatPLC), so the EnergyPlus part-load-fraction multiplier is PLF = PLR / FHeatPLC(PLR) (the D-53 transform). The grid starts at PLR 0.10 and not at 0.01: EnergyPlus floors a fuel heating coil's PLF at 0.7 (EnergyPlus::HeatingCoils::CalcFuelHeatingCoil, 25.2.0 - "PLF curve values must be >= 0.7. PLF has been reset to 0.7"), and the rational crosses 0.7 near PLR 0.055, so nodes below 0.10 would only feed the engine values it rejects. Below PLR 0.10 the Constant extrapolation holds PLF at 0.788005; the departure from the Code there is bounded by a x Fuel_rated = 1.86 % of rated fuel and is stated in D-89.
